verdict.fix_brief: The only failing gate is the required `pytest-affected`. It stopped at the first two failures (`-x`): `tests/test_agentic_exit_paths.py::test_admission_blocked_journaled_once_per_change` and `tests/test_agentic_loop_state.py::test_run_stamps_slot_freed_at_on_drop`. Both concern queue slot and admission accounting, and a targeted rerun reproduced both, so this is not a flake. The SPEC-0394 diff does not touch `queue.py`, `profiles.py` or `divergence.py` (AC9). The spec's own Test record says 9 tests in this slot/admission family (these two plus others) fail the same way on an unmodified `git archive HEAD` copy. The most likely cause is the base commit 6e66fcda ("SPEC-0395 GATING campaigns do not count against profile slots"), which changed slot accounting without updating those tests. The persona work itself looks sound: spec-lint passes and 813 tests passed. I have no shell and did not rerun the tests on the base commit. A human should decide how to unblock this: (a) fix the SPEC-0395 regression or its tests on main, then rerun this campaign's gate; (b) waive these specific tests for this campaign; or (c) mark them xfail or skip with a reference to SPEC-0395. Do not edit `queue.py` or `profiles.py` in this campaign, because AC9 forbids it. If the steward authorises a test-only fix, the implementer should adjust only the two tests' expectations (the admission_blocked journal count and the `slot_freed_at` tick count) to match the SPEC-0395 semantics, and note that in `### As shipped`.
